report.answer_text:
The Word of Wisdom became a formal commitment for Latter-day Saints on September 9, 1851, and a temple recommend requirement under President Heber J. Grant in the early 1920s. (churchofjesuschrist.org)
February 27, 1833: Joseph Smith received the revelation, now Doctrine and Covenants 89. It was originally given “not by commandment or constraint.” (churchofjesuschrist.org)
September 9, 1851: At general conference, members unanimously accepted Brigham Young’s proposal to covenant to keep it. In practice, expectations about strict observance still varied for decades. (churchofjesuschrist.org)
1919–1921: Official Church sources give different dates for the temple recommend requirement. The Church History Library dates it to 1919, while the Church’s *Church History Topics* dates it to 1921. (churchhistorylibrary.churchofjesuschrist.org)

claims.sentence: The Word of Wisdom became a formal commitment for Latter-day Saints on September 9, 1851, and a temple recommend requirement under President Heber J. Grant in the early 1920s. (churchofjesuschrist.org)
claims.claim: The Word of Wisdom became a formal commitment for Latter-day Saints on September 9, 1851.
claims.label: supported

pages.label: supported

quotes.text: On 9 September 1851, some eighteen years after it was given, the Patriarch to the Church, John Smith, delivered a talk in general conference on the Word of Wisdom.
President Brigham Young arose and proposed that all Saints formally covenant to abstain from tea, coffee, tobacco, whiskey, and “all things mentioned in the Word of Wisdom”
The motion was accepted unanimously and became binding as a commandment for all Church members thereafter.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state that on 9 September 1851 Brigham Young proposed all Saints formally covenant to abstain from the Word of Wisdom items, and the motion was accepted unanimously and became binding as a commandment for all members, which matches the claim's date and formal commitment.
pages.page_reason: The page states that on 9 September 1851 Brigham Young proposed that all Saints formally covenant to abstain from the Word of Wisdom's prohibited items, the motion was accepted unanimously, and it became binding as a commandment for all members thereafter.

quotes.text: D&C 89:2. Why Does the Lord Say “Not by Commandment or Constraint”?

The reason undoubtedly why the Word of Wisdom was given—as not by ‘commandment or restraint’ was that at that time, at least, if it had been given as a commandment it would have brought every man, addicted to the use of these noxious things, under condemnation; so the Lord was merciful and gave them a chance to overcome, before He brought them under the law.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes identify D&C 89:2 as the source of the phrase "not by commandment or constraint" and state that the Word of Wisdom was given "not by 'commandment or restraint'" at that time, which backs the claim's main point with only a minor wording difference.
pages.page_reason: The page quotes Joseph F. Smith saying the Word of Wisdom was given 'as not by commandment or restraint' at that time, and the section heading asks 'Why Does the Lord Say "Not by Commandment or Constraint"?', which together support the claim about its original giving.
